title: POC scoping - Lyra Retail (timeline & milestones)
topics: POC milestones: kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout
summary: Redwood AE/SE and Lyra Retail scoped a 6-week POC focused on customer-facing recommendation inference. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy of rerank), dataset and traffic profile, benchmark plan, and a milestone timeline (kickoff, infra/access, mid-point review with benchmark results, exec readout). Next steps include sharing SOW/pricing, access checklist, and scheduling kickoff for next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alice (Redwood AE), Ben (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Raj (Lyra Head of ML), Sofia (Platform), Hiro (CTO), Leah (Product)

[00:00] Alice: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the poc timeline and milestones, just to make sure expectations align. uh quick intro, ben is our se, he'll own the benchmarks and data ingress, maya will help on success criteria and ops.
[00:18] Raj: thanks, Alice. quick context from our side: Lyra runs a product recommendations service for our mobile app, about, uh, peak 1200 rps across three regions, typical seq len 128 for session history. main goal is reduce latency to under 80 ms p50 for generate+rerank while holding or improving click-through.
[00:37] Ben: got it, thanks. when you say generate+rerank, is that a single pass then rerank with embeddings, or two separate calls?
[00:44] Raj: two calls right now. generate on a smaller model, then a reranker step using our in-house dot-product scoring. we'd like to explore an end-to-end variant on one model to save tail latency but open to hybrid.
[00:56] Sofia: security note - we need VPC peering for the POC, and all logs must stay within our account, no shared logs. we also have SOC2 and ISO requirements.
[01:06] Alice: understood, we support private connectivity and KMS integration, we'll share our security pack.
[01:10] Hiro: curious on quantization - you mentioned earlier that Redwood has quantization profiles, what's the likely impact on accuracy vs latency?
[01:18] Ben: so rough rule: int8 quant often gives 1-3% bleed in accuracy on rerank tasks but can halve latency on some GPUs depending on kernel selection. we'll run a baseline with fp16 and then an int8 variant in the benchmark.
[01:31] Leah: ok good. moving to timeline, what do you propose for milestones?
[01:36] Alice: propose a 6-week POC: week 0 kickoff and access + infra, week 1 baseline ingest and small benchmark, week 2 model tuning + batching config, week 3 mid-point review with preliminary numbers, week 4 run full production-like benchmark (peak traffic), week 5 wrap, week 6 exec readout. we can compress if needed.
[01:52] Raj: that seems fine, though we want the mid-point review earlier if possible, maybe end of week 2?
[01:58] Ben: we can move the mid-point to end of week 2; timeline becomes: kickoff, access + data sync (days 1-3), baseline run in week 1, tuning + second benchmark week 2, mid-point review at end week 2, production-scale run week 3, and then two weeks for hardening + exec prep. total 5 weeks then.
[02:17] Maya: success criteria - let's capture explicit metrics: latency p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, throughput sustaining 1200 rps with <= 10% CPU/GPU saturation margin, top-1 rerank precision >= baseline, and cost per 1M requests reduction target of 20% vs current infra. also acceptance that small quality regression up to 2% may be tolerable if lat/cost gains are significant; we'll document.
[02:40] Raj: agree on the metrics, also need a runbook for failover to our current pipeline during POC.
[02:46] Alice: yes, we'll provide a rollback strategy and fallback routing.
[02:50] Ben: about data - can you confirm whether you can provide a sampled traffic replay, or will we test on synthetic traces?
[02:56] Sofia: we can provide a 24-hour replay anonymized and a small production-sampled set with headers removed. we need an ingress mechanism - S3 or signed URL?
[03:06] Ben: S3 works best, we'll give a presigned upload and an ingest checklist. we'll also ask for schema for reranker features.
[03:12] Leah: benchmarks - we want both latency and quality. do you have a standard harness?
[03:16] Ben: yes, we'll run our internal harness (redwood-bench) - it'll run generate and rerank flows, measure per-token and end-to-end lat, and compute ranking metrics versus your ground truth. note: sometimes transcripts of our tools say redwood-bench or redwood-benchest, sorry for the audio artifacts.
[03:31] Raj: about environment - are we doing Dedicated or Private for the POC? we prefer private deployment in our VPC for data controls.
[03:39] Alice: we can run a Private deployment in your account for the POC, or a dedicated-hosted instance with VPC peering. Private in your account means you manage the VPC but we provide the control plane; Dedicated is faster to stand up. Pros/cons: Private gives max isolation and easier compliance signoffs; Dedicated is quicker and still supports KMS.
[04:00] Hiro: provisioning time?
[04:02] Ben: Dedicated demo environment can be ready in 3-5 business days if quotas are approved. Private will take 7-14 days typically for infra setup and network approvals.
[04:12] Leah: cost visibility - what will we see in the console during POC?
[04:16] Maya: we surface token-level cost, model-level breakdown, and route usage. we'll share a live dashboard during the mid-point and final reviews.
[04:24] Raj: benchmarks - can you run a quantized int8 vs fp16 comparison and show cost per million and latency percentiles?
[04:30] Ben: yes, that's part of our standard benchmark matrix. also we can show batching configs and caching impacts; KW cache - so sorry kv cache - will be part of the analysis. sometimes speech has kv as 'kayvee' which is fun.
[04:44] Alice: action items and next steps - we'll capture these and follow up.
[04:48] Alice: rough list: 1) SOW/pricing and POC S3 ingest instructions from Redwood, 2) Lyra to share anonymized 24h traffic sample + feature schema, 3) schedule kickoff for next Tue (2026-06-16) pending signoff, 4) Redwood to provision dedicated/private options and estimate lead time.
[05:05] Raj: sounds good. also can you share the security pack and SOC2 evidence?
[05:09] Alice: yes, we'll send the security pack; for SOC2 we'll share attestation and an anonymized audit summary, along with KMS integration docs.
[05:17] Leah: can we get a short appendix on rollback and fallback latency, basically what happens if a route degrades?
[05:23] Ben: we'll include automatic fallback policy options: route to smaller model variant, route to dedicated pool, or fallback to your old pipeline. we'll document expected added latency for each.
[05:33] Maya: let's confirm stakeholders for the mid-point review: Raj, Hiro, Leah, plus product ops and our exec sponsor.
[05:40] Raj: exec sponsor will be myself and Hiro, ok.
[05:44] Alice: final recap: Proposed POC timeline (compressed to 5 weeks): Kickoff 2026-06-16, Week1 baseline + ingestion, Week2 tuning + mid-point review (end of week2), Week3 production-scale benchmark, Week4 hardening + final run, Week5 exec readout - target week of 2026-07-20 for exec readout.
[06:04] Raj: that's acceptable.
[06:06] Alice: anything else?
[06:08] Sofia: confirm VPN or VPC peering preferences in the checklist - we'll pick after we see the access doc.
[06:13] Alice: great, we'll share the access checklist and SOW by Tuesday morning.
[06:17] Ben: I'll draft the benchmark matrix and share the harness link (drive.google.com/..../redwood-bench).
[06:22] Alice: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with meeting notes and next steps.
[06:25] Raj: thanks all.

Notes: transcription has occasional misheard acronyms (KV/kv/kayvee), and some names may be slightly off in auto-caption.
